wa_steel_pulse_2.notes: Looks mossy from below but most of it is 5.8. A short slab traverse past three bolts leads into a right-facing, right-leaning corner; where the crack tapers off, leave it for a thin flake protected by two more bolts to the anchor. Cruxes are bolted, gear is good elsewhere; best on cool, dry days. A single 60 m rope reaches the ground from this anchor.
Slab crux right off the belay, around the first bolt, trending to the left end of a small overlap. A second, balancy crux on a short slab just below the bolted anchor.

Start up good layback cracks, then onto the upper slab. After the first slab bolt a hidden pocket takes a #2 cam; two more bolts protect the 5.10c crux, and gear protects the easier top. The rappel back to the P2 anchor is not a plumb line — do not swing into the gully.
